content:
A wire bent into a square of side 10 cm is reshaped into a rectangle of length 12 cm. Does that sentence instantly say "same perimeter, breadth 8" to your child? Then this chapter is in good shape. Take the free IMO Class 7 Perimeter and Area online test below. It has 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Every answer comes with a worked explanation. Aim for 8 out of 10.

What the IMO asks from Perimeter and Area in Class 7

  • Perimeter and area of squares, rectangles, parallelograms and triangles.
  • Area of paths and borders.
  • Circumference and area of circles.
  • Cost-based problems (fencing, tiling).
  • Reshaping problems: same wire, new figure.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Area of a parallelogram = base × height — the SLANT side is not the height.
  • Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height.
  • Circumference = 2πr; area = πr² — with r doubled, area becomes 4×.
  • Same wire = same perimeter, almost never the same area.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Using the slant side of a parallelogram as its height.
  • Mixing units (metres for length, cm for breadth) inside one formula.
  • Doubling area when the radius doubles.

questions.explanation: 2(3x + x) = 8x = 80 gives x = 10. Length 30 cm, breadth 10 cm.
